name: Piccolo Banda Peperomia
description: Peperomia albovittata 'Piccolo Banda', often sold as Peacock Peperomia, is a compact evergreen cultivar in the Piperaceae family. It forms a low bushy mound with thick, semi-succulent leaves that are light green with a silver cast and bold dark purple-brown veins, plus pinkish-red stems. The striking leaf patterning gives it its peacock nickname. It prefers bright indirect light and will scorch in harsh direct sun; it also tolerates lower and artificial light, making it a good desk or shelf plant. Allow the top 2–5 cm of soil to dry between waterings—overwatering is the main risk. Average household humidity (about 40–60%) is fine; warm rooms around 18–29 °C suit it best. Tiny flower spikes may appear but are not showy. Non-toxic to cats, dogs, and humans. Propagate from stem or leaf cuttings.
careTips: Provide bright indirect light; avoid harsh direct sun which scorches the leaves
Tolerates lower light and fluorescent office lighting, though colors are best in brighter conditions
Water only when the top 2–5 cm of soil is dry; semi-succulent leaves store moisture
Use a well-draining mix with perlite or bark; never leave the pot sitting in water
Average room humidity (40–60%) is sufficient; avoid cold drafts and temperatures below about 15 °C
Keep temperatures roughly 18–29 °C; protect from heaters and sudden temperature swings
Fertilize lightly every 4–6 weeks in spring and summer at half strength
Propagate from stem or leaf cuttings; watch for mealybugs
Non-toxic and safe for homes with pets
geographicOrigin: Cultivar of tropical American Peperomia albovittata (often attributed to Dutch breeding)
